subject: Q1 close: consolidated scorecard and exec summary for QBR
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Dobbs <sara.dobbs@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q1 close: consolidated scorecard and exec summary for QBR

Team — attaching the consolidated Q1 scorecard and a first-pass narrative for the Exec QBR next week. High level: we hit 3/5 stretch targets, 7/10 core KR thresholds, and one notable regression on inference latency (p95 up 18% month-over-month) that we need to own in the narrative.

What I need from you by EOD:
- Quick pass on the numbers tab in the scorecard (Q1_2026_OKR_scorecard.xlsx) — call out any corrections to actuals.
- Tone edits to the narrative where noted (QBR_narrative_v2.docx) — there are two inline comments on the latency section and on the Customer Expansion story.
- Confirm which two slides you want highlighted in the exec deck (I put proposed slide IDs in the notes column of the scorecard).

Context on the latency regression: this is primarily a model-serving throughput/queueing effect tied to a burst of large-sequence workflows in mid-March. We have a mitigation plan (KV-cache tuning + temporary routing to larger instances) but it will show up in the QBR as a risk item unless we close the loop.

I copied Sara from Acme — she shared a short client note that we can surface as a quote if we choose (see drive link).

Attachments: Q1_2026_OKR_scorecard.xlsx (numbers + proposed scores), QBR_narrative_v2.docx (narrative + comments), QBR_slides_draft.pdf (slide placeholders)

Thanks — please reply with your final score adjustments or a one-line approval.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q1 close: consolidated scorecard and exec summary for QBR

Evelyn — quick read done. Two small adjustments from my side:
1) Objective: Platform reliability — I think the KR for p99 availability should be 99.95% (not 99.9%) in the final doc; our infra leads confirmed 99.95 is the correct target for the quarter.
2) Customer story: change the Acme quote to the shorter version on the drive (line 4) — the long quote reads as product marketing language.

On the latency regression: agree we should include the mitigation steps but avoid technical minutiae in the exec deck. Suggest we show a one-slide timeline (Incident → Mitigation → Plan) with owner = Marcus.

I'll mark those edits in QBR_narrative_v2.docx and approve numbers once the availability value is updated.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — I've reviewed and left a few inline edits. A couple of items to call out:
- For the latency regression narrative, propose we frame it as a capacity-profile mismatch (workload mix shift) and call out the short-term routing fallback we used. That reduces perceived product instability and centers the ask on capacity/config.
- For the Cost Efficiency objective: I recommend we present the score as 8/10 (showing improvement from last quarter) but include a footnote that unit-cost gains were concentrated in batch/embedding workloads.
- I'll draft a 2-sentence executive summary for slide 2 that reads: "Platform steady progress on throughput and cost; targeted remediation underway for mid-March latency spike." Use unless someone objects.

Also +1 to Laura's one-slide timeline — Marcus please own it.

— Vivek

CTO | Redwood Inference

I'm okay with Vivek's recommendation for 8/10; propose we include a concrete data point (e.g., normalized token cost by workload) in the appendix rather than inflating the headline.

On the timeline slide: I'll include short bullets for detection → mitigation → follow-up and will attach the incident runbook excerpt as a backup slide.

Also, for the Acme quote: Sara asked that we include attribution (Acme, senior product lead) if we use it in the exec deck — she flagged that in the note I saw on Drive.

- Availability target corrected to 99.95% (per Laura).
- Cost Efficiency score set to 8/10 (per Vivek + Marcus).
- Latency regression will be framed as a capacity-profile mismatch with a one-slide timeline; Marcus to own timeline + backup runbook slide.
- Use the shorter Acme quote and include attribution as requested by Sara (Acme, Senior Product Lead).

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: Timeline slide + backup runbook excerpt (due Wed 03/31 EOD).
- Vivek: Two-sentence exec summary for slide 2 (due Wed 03/31 noon).
- Laura: Confirm customer quote line & final sign-off on narrative (due Wed 03/31 EOD).
- Evelyn: Produce final PDF deck and distribute to execs + board (target Thu 04/01 morning).

Attachments: final_scorecard attached (Q1_2026_OKR_scorecard.xlsx), final narrative (QBR_narrative_v2.docx), slides draft (QBR_slides_draft.pdf). I've also dropped the Acme note to the drive link above.

Dry-run: Let's meet Thursday 04/01 09:00 PT for a 20-minute dry run. Calendar invite sent.

Thanks — feel free to flag any last-minute issues in thread.
